transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?
I came in because I’ve been feeling really wound up most of the day. It’s like my body is bracing for something, even when I’m just sitting at my computer or trying to relax after dinner.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about different things in your life, like work, family, or health, even when there isn’t a clear reason to worry?

Yes, I do. My mind kind of jumps from one worry to the next. I’ll be thinking about my sister in Arecibo, then whether I missed something at work, then my husband driving home, or church commitments, or bills. A lot of the time there isn’t an actual problem yet, but I’m already trying to prepare for what could go wrong.
Do you find it hard to control or stop the worrying once it starts, even when you know the thoughts might not make sense?

Yes, that’s been hard. I’ll tell myself, “Daniela, enough, just focus on this report,” but then one small worry turns into five more. Before I realize it, I’ve spent half an hour checking messages or going over everything that could go wrong. It’s frustrating because I know I’m not helping anything, but it’s hard to stop.
Have you noticed any physical symptoms, like restlessness, muscle tension, or feeling fatigued, that seem to go along with these anxious thoughts?
Yes. I feel restless and tense a lot of the day. It’s like I’m wound up or bracing for something, even if I’m just sitting at my computer or trying to relax after dinner.
Do you feel worried or anxious more days than not, and has this been going on for a while, like most days over the past several months?

Yes, it’s been more days than not. I’d say it’s been going on for about thirteen months now, since my sister in Arecibo started needing a lot more help from the family. Since then it just feels like the worry has been there most days.

Have you ever experienced sudden episodes where you feel intense fear or discomfort that peaks within a few minutes, like your heart racing, shortness of breath, or feeling like something terrible is about to happen?
I don’t think so. I mean, I get anxious and tense, but I haven’t noticed sudden attacks like that where it peaks really fast or feels like something terrible is happening.
Do you find that your anxiety and worry occur more days than not and tend to be about a variety of events or activities, rather than just one specific thing?

Yes, it’s definitely more days than not. And it’s not just one thing. My mind kind of jumps around—my sister in Arecibo, something I might’ve missed at work, my husband driving home, church commitments, bills. I find myself getting ready for problems that haven’t even happened.
Do you find that you have trouble concentrating or staying focused because your mind is preoccupied with worries?

Yes, I do. I’ll try to tell myself, “Daniela, enough, focus on this report,” but then one small worry turns into five more. Before I know it, I’ve spent half an hour checking messages or replaying what could go wrong instead of doing what I’m supposed to be doing.
Do you have trouble falling asleep or staying asleep because your mind is racing or you’re feeling anxious?

Yes. Most nights I do fall asleep eventually, but I wake up around three or four in the morning and my mind starts going—like about my sister’s next appointment, or some server issue at work. Even if I’ve technically slept enough hours, I wake up feeling like I didn’t really rest.
